For every $100 of sales, $63.75 went to the cost of the seed itself and $44.35 to selling and admin — together more than revenue — so the quarter ended $51.17 in the red per $100, funded from the balance sheet.

oneTimers: Separation costs ($99M in Q3; $228M in the first nine months): legal, advisory and standalone-setup costs from the October 1 spin-off out of Corteva. Excluded from Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA.
Restructuring and asset-related charges, net: a $1M net credit in Q3 ($31M charge year-to-date).
A further ~$21M of one-time separation expenses are expected after the separation, per the release — not yet in these numbers.

Amortization of intangibles ($120M in Q3): a recurring non-cash charge on intangibles carried over from the DowDuPont/Corteva separation — excluded from adjusted EPS, but it recurs every quarter until the assets are fully amortized.

GAAP vs adjusted gap: a GAAP net loss of $480M vs an Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA loss of $269M. The bridge is mostly separation costs ($99M), amortization ($120M), R&D ($268M) and the tax benefit.
otherDetail: Other expense, net of $10M plus $34M of interest expense on the new standalone capital structure — a combined $44M outside operating income.

takeaways.text: Q3 is the seasonally smallest quarter — most seed is sold in the first half — but the $480M GAAP loss still widened from $391M a year ago as $99M of separation costs hit and R&D rose 14% to $268M. Even excluding spin-off costs, adjusted operating EBITDA was a $269M loss, 33% worse than last year.
takeaways.title: A loss quarter is normal for seed — but this one was deeper

takeaways.text: Volume fell 9% — lower corn acres in North America and Europe (drought), delayed monsoons in India, and the shift to a licensing model for Brazil soybeans — but price/mix rose 6% on demand for the latest hybrids and more licensing income. Corn sales still grew 4% to $607M; soybeans fell 26% to $133M.
takeaways.title: Prices rose while volumes fell

takeaways.text: Year-to-date pro forma sales are up 4% to $8.53B with $1.01B of net income, and management reaffirmed full-year adjusted operating EBITDA of ~$2.8B and adjusted EPS of $2.25–$2.35. The board also started a $0.13 quarterly dividend and a $3B buyback — a standalone company acting like one.
takeaways.title: The full year still points up

verdict: Vylor's first quarter as a standalone seed company was a $480 million loss, as a seasonally small third quarter collided with $99 million of spin-off costs and weather-hit volumes, even as prices rose 6% and full-year guidance was reaffirmed.
